reason: The hypothesis relies on Ti and Si synergy for protective oxide formation, but the cited evidence does not directly support this in the specific alloy system. E1 discusses Si for corrosion resistance and passivation in FeCoNiCr systems, not oxidation at high temperature. E2 and E3 concern Ti and Si effects in Nb-silicide-based refractory alloys, which differ fundamentally in composition and oxidation mechanisms from the fcc HEA. The leap from these references to the proposed mechanism is unsupported by specific prior evidence.
premises: Ti and Si synergistically promote a protective oxide layer in HEAs
Ti is key for oxidation resistance in complex alloys
Si enhances passivation film formation and corrosion resistance in HEAs
The cited evidence on Nb-silicide and refractory alloys applies to the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni-Ti fcc HEA system
